content.text: In the Philippines, digital creators face a significant challenge: most online [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-infrastructure-south-asian-creators-broken-here-infrastructure|payment]] platforms are unavailable or severely restricted, making it difficult to sell digital products to international buyers. The problem is not unique to the Philippines, but rather a broader issue affecting creators in Africa, the Middle East, and other regions where Stripe, PayPal, and other payment gateways are blocked. This post provides a quick-win solution for Filipino digital creators to get payment methods working today, without relying on servers or expensive infrastructure.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What You Can Actually Get Done Today

You can actually get [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-how-start-selling-digital-products-crypto-works-4|How How]]ed with a sovereign digital commerce stack today, using free and open-source tools that do not require any server infrastructure. You can host your digital store on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, process payments with NOWPayments, and deliver files through [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/google-apps-script-digital-commerce-automation-explained-digital-4|COREMERCH guide to google]] Drive or Cloudflare R2. This minimum viable stack can get you up and running in under an hour, without any upfront costs or complicated setup.
The Minimum Viable Stack That Works

The minimum viable stack consists of GitHub Pages for hosting, NOWPayments for payment processing, and Google Drive for file delivery. You can also use Cloudflare Pages instead of GitHub Pages, and Cloudflare R2 instead of Google Drive. This stack is free, open-source, and does not require any server infrastructure. You can deploy it in under an hour, and start selling digital products to international buyers.
Skipping the Steps That Do Not Matter Yet

You do not need to worry about setting up a Stripe account, or integrating PayPal with your store. You can skip the steps that require a server, and focus on getting your digital commerce stack up and running. This is the most important step, and it will get you started with a sovereign digital commerce stack that you can scale as needed.
You can sell digital products internationally, without relying on servers or expensive infrastructure.
Getting Your First Transaction Live

Creators in Ethiopia, Cameroon, Tanzania, Venezuela, Zimbabwe, and the Philippines face a compounded challenge: not only are conventional payment platforms unavailable, but local banking infrastructure may add additional friction to receiving international transfers through alternative channels. Crypto payments remove this layer entirely. A seller in Addis Ababa and a seller in Amsterdam receive USDT transactions through the same NOWPayments infrastructure, at the same speed, with the same 0.5% fee. The blockchain has no knowledge of which country a wallet is located in. The webhook fires to both backends identically. Geographic neutrality is not a feature — it is the fundamental property of how blockchains work.
What to Do in the Next 24 Hours

The Edge Commerce Stack that COREMERCH deploys most frequently combines Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling and order processing, Supabase for order storage, Resend for transactional email delivery, and NOWPayments for crypto payment verification. The total monthly cost is zero. The scale ceiling is significantly higher than what most individual creators need — Cloudflare Workers handles 100,000 requests per day on the free tier, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage, and Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month. For a creator in any country on earth, this stack provides the same infrastructure as a well-funded e-commerce operation at no monthly cost.

Yes, you can sell digital products internationally, without relying on servers or expensive infrastructure. You can use a sovereign digital commerce stack that consists of free and open-source tools, and deploy it in under an hour. This will get you started with a working digital commerce stack that you can scale as needed.
